minutes_text:
CITY  OF SOUTH  GATE
  REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY,  JULY  8, 2025

CALL  TO ORDER  Maria  Davila,  Mayor  called  a Regular  City  Council  Meeting  to order at
  6:46 p.m.

INVOCATION  Steve Costley,  Director  Parks & Recreation

PLEDGE  OFALLEGIANCE  Raul F. Salinas,  City Attorney

ROLL  CALL  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor  Maria  Davila,  Vice  Mayor  Joshua Barron,  Council  Member  Maria
  del Pilar Avalos,  Council  Member  Gil Hurtado  and Council  Member  Al
  Rios;  City Treasurer  Jose De La Paz, City Attorney  Raul F. Salinas,
  Assistant  City  Manager  Arturo  Cervantes

EXCUSED/ABSENT  City  Manager  Rob Houston

l
COMMUNITY  DEV/

HOUSING  Following  the conclusion  of the Public  Hearing,  the City  Council:

  a.  Adopted  Resolution  No. 2025-22-CC  Resolution  of the City  Council
  of the City  of South  Gate, California,  receiving  and approving  the
  Five-Year  2025-2029  Consolidated  Plan and Fiscal  Year 2025-2026
  Annual  Action  Plan;

  b.  Authorizing  the City  Manager,  or designee,  to submit  to the U.S.
  Department  of Housing  and Urban  Development  the Five-Year  2025-
  2029 Consolidated  Plan and FY 2025-2026  Annual  Action  Plan (as
  amended);  and

  c.  Authorizing  the City  Manager,  or designee,  to enter into agreements
  with  eligible  subrecipients  in a form  acceptable  to the City Attorney.

  Carol Averell,  Housing  Manager,  gave the presentation.

  Mayor  Davila  asked if anyone  in the audience  wished  to speak on this
  item.  Seeing  no one step forward;  Mayor  Davila  closed  the audience
  portion.

EMAILS  Mario  Dominguez  urges the City  Council  to allocate  CDBG  funding  to the
  Department  of Parks and Recreation.
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JTJLY  8, 2025

COMM[iNITY  DEV /

HOUSING  CONT'D  Edgar  Pelayo  advocates  for the CDBG  funding  to be used for the Parks
  and Recreation  Department.

RECESS  Prior  to the conclusion  of item 1, the City  Council  recessed  at 7:00 p.m.,
  and reconvened  at 8:57 p.m., with  all Members  of Council  present.

  Council  MemberAvalos  questioned  how this business  has been conducted
  for the last five years. There  is information  attached  to the staff report  as to
  how the CAC  allocated  the funds  back in February.

  Ms. Averell  stated the item went before  the CAC  for their
  recommendations,  but HUD  had not released  the allocations  until  May.

  Mr. Salinas  asked Ms. Averell  to explain  the posting  notice.

  Ms. Averell  stated that once the allocations  are received,  the city prepares
  the documents  and then posts the consolidated  plan  and aru'iual action  plan
  on June 5'h because  there is 30-day  notice  for public  review  requirement.

  Council  MemberAvalos  has an issue as to how these funds  were allocated.
  There  is an item for $12,000  and asked the meaning  of "other  CDBG
  activities,"  and can that funding  be used for food  insecurity.

  Ms. Averell  stated the food programs  fall under  the public  service  grants.
  The public  service  grants have a cap of 15%  and during  the presentation  it
  was mentioned  the amount  was maximized.  The CAC  makes  these
  recommendations;  however,  the City  Council  can make  any changes  to the
  recornrnendations.

  Council  MemberAvalos  asked if the $12,000  can be allocated  into food
  insecurity  due to the need.

  Ms. Averell  stated not for the food insecurity  because  it falls under the
  public  service  grants.  The council  can move  funds  within  that 15% cap
  under the public  service  grants.  The only  amount  that can be utilized  for
  public  service  grants  is $178,895.

  Council  Member  Avalos  asked if the $12,000  can be allocated  directly  to
  the businesses  that have been heavily  impacted?

  Ms. Averell  stated if it's economic  development,  yes.

  Council  Member  Avalos  would  like to make an amendment  to ensure that
  the $12,000  be allocated  to the small  businesses  that have been impacted
  due to the current  situation.

COMMUNITY  DEV/

HOUSING  CONT'D  Ms. Averell  stated Ana Marie  LeNoue  is present,  and she can clarify.

  Ms. LeNoue  stated that the South  Gate Women's  Business  Center,  is the
  Chamber  of Commerce  application.  She also stated that within  the dollars
  that are mentioned  on the staff report,  $12,000,  $451,000, and $513,990
  can be distributed  to a business  assistance  grant program.

  Mayor  Davila  prefers  to allocate  funds from  another  program.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  suggested  the neighborhood  revitalization
  progmm.

  Council  Member  Avalos  wants  to make certain  the $12,000  will  be
  allocated  to all businesses,  not just members.

  Ms. LeNoue  stated that this is a new program  the Chamber  is presenting  to
  the city.

  Mayor  Davila  suggested  taking  $15,000  from  the neighborhood
  revitalization  program  and leaving  $400,000.  Use the $15,000  for the
  businesses.

  Council  Member  Avalos  suggested  $75,000  because  there are a lot of
  businesses  that have been impacted.  She knows  of at least five businesses
  that are closing  at the end of July.

  Ms. Averell  and Ms. LeNoue's  recommendation  for allocating  funds  from
  the neighborhood  revitalization  and the street and sidewalk  improvement
  project.

  Mr. Cervantes  stated in public  works,  we are overseeing  the streets and
  sidewalks  citywide.  We have a plan that calls for over $80 million  in street
  improvements  needed.  Sidewalk  improvements  are due to sidewalk  issues
  throughout  the city. He recommends  preserving  the $513,990.

  Council  Member  Avalos  asked if we could  allocate  fiinding  from  the
  neighborhood  revitalization  program,  $75,000  or $50,000?

  Ms. Averell  stated yes, some funding  can be allocated.

  Vice Mayor  Barron  asked for an example  of what that program  does.

  Ms. LeNoue  stated that the program  is similar  to the home  funded
  residential  rehabilitation  program  except  there are different  requirements
  for CDBG  funded  rehab versus  the home rehab.  Under  the CDBG.

  Page 3 of 12
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JULY  8, 2025

l
COMMUNITY  DEV/

HOUSING  CONT'D  Mr. Salinas  asked given  that the administration  didn't  finalize  these
  numbers  until  May,  was the deadline  extended  for the city to approve  of
  this?

  Ms. LeNoue  stated that the deadline  originally  every year is May  15fh. The
  allocation  numbers  were issued May 12"1 or the 14".  Then the city is given
  60 days to finalize  the product  that is before  the City  Council.  The
  deadline  is this Friday.  The city is planning  to submit  this on Friday
  pending  approval.

  Mr. Salinas  asked if the City  Council  did not approve  this item tonight,
  does the city loses the money.

  Ms. LeNoue  stated the city would  not lose the money  until  August  16I11.

  Vice  Mayor  Barron  asked if City  Council  makes  any changes,  it has to be
  posted  as a change  and it must come to City  Council.

  Ms. LeNoue  stated the City  Council  can make  changes  tonight  because  it
  is a public  hearing.

  Mayor  Davila  asked Councilwoman  Avalos  how much  is she asking  for?

  Council  Member  Avalos  was asking  for $75,000  for businesses  that are in
  dire need.

  Mayor  Davila  stated there must be requirements.

  Council  Member  Avalos  asked about requirements.

  Ms. LeNoue  recornrnended  allocating  funds  for the program  and then staff
  will  work  to develop  guidelines  and return  to City  Council  for approval.

  Council  Member  Avalos  suggested  at least fifteen  businesses  can be
  helped  with  $1,000.

  Mayor  Davila  asked when  the businesses  would  be able to use the funds.
  How  long would  it take for staff to develop  guidelines.

  Ms. LeNoue  stated the city implemented  a business  assistance  program
  with  CDBGCV  funds  with  the pandemic  money.  Staff can go back to
  those regulations/  guidelines.  The direction  from  City  Council  is to assist
  businesses  that are struggling  due to the immigrant  community  not being
  able to come out and shop local.

  Page 4 of 12
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF JTJLY  8, 2025

l
COMMUNITY  DEV/

HOUSING  CONT'D  Council Member Hurtado  directed  to also demonstrate  that there has been
  a negative impact.

  Ms. LeNoue  asked for staff guidance  from  the City  Council  what  would
  be the level  of criteria  so staff can explore  and return  with  those
  guidelines.

  Council  MemberAvalos  stated that businesses  were generating  on average
  $5,000 gain in a month  and now they are at $2,000,  an extra $1,000  would
  come in handy  to keep the business  open or employees  that they already
  have.

  Mayor  Davila  asked if it is first  come,  first  serve then the businesses  that
  are impacted  won't  be receiving  any 'funds.

  Mr. Salinas  stated that the City  Manager  suggested  allowing  staff to work
  out the details  and since we have until  August  16".

  Ms. LeNoue  stated the deadline  is July 13I11,but staff are submitting  on the
  1 Ith if it is permitted.  The deadline  to lose the funds  is August.

  Council  MemberAvalos  stated making  a friendly  amendment  allocating
  $50,000  for economic  development  and staff will  work  on logistics.

  Ms. LeNoue  stated for clarification  purposes  because  specification  is
  needed,  it would  be for small  business  assistance  program.  And  then return
  to City  Council  with  the guidelines.  That would  be outside  of the  money

  piece.  The money  piece is part of the con plan and action  plan.

  Council  Member  Avalos  replied  yes.

  Mr. Salinas  stated that the motion  would  be to amend the neighborhood
  revitalization  program  by allocating  $50,000  from  the neighborhood
  revitalization  program  and direct  staff to come up with  guidelines
  consistent  with  what has been discussed  for disadvantaged  businesses  in
  the city and make  sure it is consistent  with  federal  law.

  Council  Member  Avalos  wants  to make sure that the funds the chamber
  receives  are opened  to all small  businesses  in South  Gate, not just to
  members.  She would  also like to meet withAnna  and inquire  what the
  chamber  is doing  for South  Gate businesses  that are struggling  due to
  people  not shopping.

  Ms. LeNoue  stated the following  changes  would  stay the same except  for
  the neighborhood  revitalization  program  would  drop down  to $365,000
  and would  add a small  business  assistance  grant program  at $50,000.

HOUSING  CONT'D  Staff's  recommendation  was unanimously  approved  (as amended)  by
  motion  of Council  Member  Avalos  and seconded  by Council  Member
  Hurtado.

  ROLL  CALL:  Council  Member  Avalos,  yes; Council  Member  Hurtado,
  yes; Council  Member  Rios,  yes; Vice  Mayor  Barron,  yes; Mayor  Davila,
  yes.

COMMENTS  FROM  THE
AUDIENCE  - NON-AGENDA

ITEMS  Vicky,  South Gate resident,  was disappointed  with  the cancellation  of the
  celebration  for the 4'h of July at the park.  She understands  the iSsues with
  the immigration  law, but South  Gate residents  had the right  to participate
  in the celebration  for the 4'h of July.

  Alice  Cueto,  South  Gate resident,  was disappointed  that the 4"1 of July
  celebration  was canceled.  She feels for the vendors  that lost income  on
  that day.

  Lizette  Ruiz,  Kauffman  Ave, commanded  the city for cancelling  the event.
  She once again is asking  the police  department  to enforce  the law against
  masked  individuals  with  no ICE identification.  She is part of the AB617
  Community  Steering  Group,  which  focuses  on lowering  emissions  in our
  regions  of Southeast  LA and isn't  certain  if the city received  an email  from
  Solace or Assembly  Member  asking  for letters  of support  because they are
  running  out of funding.

  Alyssa  Gomez  is a case manager  providing  field-based  mental  health
  services  so the SELA  community.  She is urging  City  Council  to follow
  Huntington  Park's  lead in enacting  a city  ordinance  that declares  itself  a
  sanctuary  city.

EMAILS  Mario  Dominguez  urges the City  Council  to pursue  a regional  park open
  space district  competitive  Measure  A grants  this July to fund the planning
  and design  of a splash pad at South  Gate Park.

  Thomas  Buckley  expressed  concerns  that the South Gate City  Clerk's
  Office  is ignoring  his public  records  request  emails.

  Edgar  Pelayo  expresses  concern  that the City  Council  and staff are not
  treating  the city's  budget  deficit  with  the urgency  it deserves.  He criticized
  the current  approach  of relying  on residents  to cover the shortfall  through
  increased  taxes, fees, and services  that were  cut. He urges the City  Council
  to consider  all options  such as outsourcing  contract  renegotiations  and re-
  evaluating  pay raises and prioritizing  the needs of South  Gate residents
  over special  interests.

  Page 6 of 12
   REGULAR  CITY  COUNCIL  MEETING  MINUTES  OF .nJLY  8, 2025

EMAILS  CON'TD  Roberto  Sanchez  expressed  frustration  over the city's  financial  situation
  and the poor  condition  of the South  Gate's  infrastructure  questioning  who
  is responsible  for the neglect.  He also criticized  the decision  to spend
  money  on horses.  He has no confidence  in long-serving  Council  Members
  and believes  new competent  leadership  is needed  to restore  the city.

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS

FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS  Steve Costley,  Director  of Parks and Recreation,  stated that the first
  successful  concert  at the park was held last on Thursday.  Mariachi  Divas
  played.  About  450 people  showed  up. He also stated that this Saturday,
  July 12'h at 10:00  a.m. will  be the grand opening  of the newest  park,  the
  Urban  Orchard.  The Aru"iual  Fun Run is taking  place on Saturday,  July  Igth
  at 10:00  a.m.

  Gabriel  Perez, Director  of Community  Development,  nothing  to report.

  Luis  Frausto,  Director  of Administrative  Services,  the staff is continuing  to
  work  on the budget  and hopes to present  an updated  budget  for
  consideration  on July 22nd. He looks  forward  to meeting  with  the Ad Hoc
  Committee

  Jon Hamilton,  Director  of Human  Resources,  nothing  to report.

  Chief  Arakawa  stated that he bears most of the responsibility  for
  cancelling  the fireworks  show. He had received  information  of potential
  protests  countywide.  He prefers  to get criticized  for cancelling  versus
  getting  criticized  a'fter the fact that he was ill-prepared  to protect  the city
  and the citizens.

  Chief  Arakawa  mentioned  an incident  that happened  in area 5 on Main
  Street the day before  the 4th of July. The South  Gate Police  Department
  investigated  where  30 tons of fireworks  were seized. The fire department
  was called  for assistants,  public  works  and Mr. C's Towing  were also
  helping.  Five people  were taken  into custody.  He apologized  to the
  residents  who were temporarily  displaced  for several  hours. An evacuation
  had to be done due to the volatile  nature  of the fireworks.  Restitution  will
  be requested  during  the criminal  court proceedings  to reimburse  the city
  for all the costs.

  Chief  Arakawa  stated that an agenda item will  be presented  at the next
  council  meeting  regarding  the police  department  being  awarded  $100,000
  grant from  the California  Highway  Patrol  to enforce  impaired  driving,
  marijuana  impairment  and it includes  the purchase  of a vehicle  to be used
  for the traffic  division.

  Mayor  Davila  thanked  the police  department  and everyone  that worked  to
  remove  the fireworks  from  the city.

REPORTS  AND  COMMENTS
FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS

CONT'D  Arturo  Cervantes,  Assistant  City  Manager/Director  of Public  Works,  stated
  that Circle  Park is being  renovated  and completion  is expected  at the end
  of this month.  Another  project  is residential  resurfacing.

  Rail  F. Salinas,  City Attorney  stated the time  that it's taken to respond  to a
  certain  public  record  act request.  It's  a unique  time period  that the city has
  taken for this, but it involves  reviewing  electronic  records,  which  require  a
  bit of review  time.  It is not a function  of the City  Clerk's  Office  or their
  failure  to try to move these along.  He replied  to the requesting  party  this
  a'Jternoon.  He also explained  the reason  for cancelling  the fireworks.

  Jose De La Paz, City Treasurer,  nothing  to report.

  Yodit  Glaze,  City  Clerk,  nothing  to report.

  Council  Member  Avalos  thanked  the community  for attending  tonight's
  Council  Meeting  and on YouTube.  She understands  the concern  about
  cancelling  an event as the 4Ih of July, but given  what happened  yesterday
  in MacArthur  Park, she would  not put this community  in harm's  way.

  Council  MemberAvalos  was in Portland  representing  the educators  of the
  State of California,  and the NEA  President,  Becky  Pringle,  is going  back
  to Washington,  D.C.  and reminding  Congress  that took money  from  the
  union,  that the teachers  don't  forget.  She acla'iowledged  and gave credit  to
  a local nonprofit,  Compatior  because  they are committed  to the City  of
  South  Gate.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  remembered  sometime  in the 1980's  he was
  doing  some research,  and he ran across an event that took place in 1954
  called  Operation  Wetback,  Dwight  D. Eisenhower  was President  at the
  time,  and everyone  was getting  departed  people  of color,  Mexicans
  (whether  born here or not).  He was thinking  we won't  have to go through
  that again and here we are, history  is repeating  itself.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  stated the city  is a municipality,  it is at the
  lowest  level.  It's the Federal  Government,  State, County  and then the
  cities.  He has reached  out to the state, Gavin  Newsome's  Office,  an
  assembly  member,  state senator  and they are all trying  everything,
  lawsuits.

  Council  Member  Rios thanked  the community  for attending  tonight's
  Council  Meeting.  Thanked  the chief  for his explanation.  It is important  for
  the community  to understand  the dynamic.  He asked if ICE communicated
  with  the police  department.

  Chief  Arakawa  stated there has been no communication  with  ICE.

FROM  CITY  OFFICIALS

CONT'D  Council  Member  Rios  stated  this  country  is made  of immigrants.  He
  wondering  if the city  can use ARPA  funds  to help  the community.  He
  questioned  why  trees need to be removed  and/or  cut down.

  Council  MemberAvalos  understands  Council  Member  Rios,  but she stated
  that  Long  Beach  Boulevard  between  Southern  and Long  Beach  Boulevard
  is a health  hazard.

  Mr.  Cervantes  stated  that  about  a year  or a year  and a half  ago, the city
  was experiencing  issues  with  a lot of larger  trees  coming  down,  there  were
  a lot of liability  claims  coming  in. A hazardous  assessment  review  was
  done  of all the trees  and a list of the priority  trees  for removal  based  on
  actual  hazards  was reviewed  by an arborist.  The trees that  are being
  removed  is that  last phase  of those  trees that we consider  potentially
  hazardous  that  could  come  down  during  rain  or heavy  events.

  Council  Member  Hurtado  stated  that  if anyone  needs  essentials,  Southeast
  Leadership  Network  has number.  Many  people  have  been reaching  out to
  them.  The numbers  are 562-842-6070  or 323-804-6639.

  Council  Member  Avalos  suggested  a recorded  line  for people  to call  in and
  be able to disseminate  to different  organizations  to be able to provide
  assistance.

  Vice  Mayor  Barron  thanked  the chief  for his explanation.  It was a hard
  decision  to make  and important  to always  keep  the cornrnunity  safe. He is
  a volunteer  with  the Southeast  Leadership  Network.  There  are a few
  volunteers  here that  are part of the Kiwanis,  and we do weekly  food
  boxing  events.  The  list has grown  to 150  families  all through  the southeast
  Los Angeles  area. He thanked  the non-profits  that  are finding  the resources
  that  are being  able to be provided.  A lot of these  non-profits  don't  want
  their  name  mentioned  because  they  receive  federal  funding.  He spoke
  about  the Big  Beautiful  Bill that will  provide  $140 million  to the new ICE
  agents  hired  to detain  undocumented  people.  The  federal  government
  spent  $30 million  in the month of June to arrest 1,700 undocumented,  and
  criminals.  We need to work  together  and see the accomplishments.

  Mayor  Davila  thanked  the community  for attending  tonight's  Council
  Meeting.  She concurs  with  City  Councils'  comments.  We need to work
  together  and help  families  who  are in need.  She thanked  the Southeast
  Leadership  Network  for their  help.  Thanked  her colleagues  for their  work
  and support  to the families  in need.

  Vice  Mayor  Barron  thanked  members  of the staff  for their  support  during
  this time.

CONT'D  City  Clerk  Glaze  asked for clarification  on the tree trimming.

  Mr. Cervantes  stated there is maintenance  which  includes  tree trimming  on
  all the city's  trees. On occasions,  residents  don't  want  trees to be trirnrned
  aggressively,  but the city  continues  as a normal  course  of business.  In
  terms  of trees that need to be removed  that are considered  hazardous  are
  being  removed.

CONSENT  CALENDAR  Agenda  Items  2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 were unanimously  approved  by motion
  of Council  Member  Avalos  and seconded  by Mayor  Davila.

RECESS  Prior  to the conclusion  of the Consent  Calendar,  the City  Council  recessed
  at 8:09 p.m.,  and reconvened  at 8:15 p.m., with  all Members  of Council
  present.

  ROLL  CALL:  Council  Member  Avalos,  yes; Council  Member  Hurtado,
  yes;  Council  Member  Rios, yes; Vice  Mayor  Barron,  yes; Mayor  Davila,
  yes.

  entitled  Resolution  of the City  Council  of the City  of South  Gate,
  California,  voicing  opposing  unlawful  immigration  enforcement  tactics
  that violate  federal  law and constitutional  protections  during  Consent
  Calendar.

  a.  Amendment  No. 2 to Contract  No. 2023-97-CC  with  ClientFirst
